svg.aria-label: The empty plect.status_message that a runtime writes at turn end is the single idle fact, read two ways. The idle-sleep deadline starts at an empty status written after the current run began; it elapses after sleep_after_idle with no newer inbound, and the session goes down with sleep, releasing its max_up_children slot; an inbound during the wait cancels it, and the next turn's empty status starts a new wait. The resume decision reads the previous run's last status before the new run's setup and ignores the waking inbound: an empty status suppresses plect.session.resumed for repair, wake, and up, for headless and interactive runtimes alike; a nonempty status or a runtime that never writes status gets the resume instruction as today. Only dispatched sessions, with a parent or a population admission, sleep automatically; operator-created top-level sessions, sessions with no completed turn, and workflows without sleep_after_idle never do. A headless worker whose working status write fails leaves the turn queued. The decision supersedes the PR 574 draft's idle_down_after and takes over its provenance protection, but not its session-level destroy policy or the removal of population auto_down and auto_destroy. A separate activity event or column, a headless-only idle confirmation, and the population eviction predicate for resume were not chosen.

g.text: Idle means the run's last status is the empty status
One status stream, two readers: the idle-sleep deadline and the resume decision

down --sleep

Up
reads status first
run 2 setup
new worker
sleep_after_idle elapses with no newer inbound
an inbound inside this wait cancels it; the next turn's "" starts a new one
resume decision: previous run's last status, read before run 2 setup
the waking inbound is not consulted, so an idle sleep wakes without plect.session.resumed
Sleeps automatically?
✓ dispatched: has a parent or a population admission
workflow sets sleep_after_idle; its "" has aged past it
✗ never: operator-created top-level session
no parent, no population (bare plect up); idle for any length
✗ no completed turn in the current run
no "" written after this run began, so no deadline starts
✗ workflow without sleep_after_idle
an absent duration disables automatic sleep
plect.session.resumed on repair, wake, or up?
not sent: previous run's last status is ""
headless and interactive runtimes alike, any provenance
sent: previous run's last status is nonempty
a turn was cut off; still delivered ahead of queued events
sent: the runtime never writes status
no status to read; the resume instruction arrives as today
headless worker: "working" write fails → turn stays queued
so an earlier "" never stands in for an interrupted turn
Relation to the PR #574 draft
✗ superseded: idle_down_after (automatic full down)
sleep_after_idle with down --sleep takes its place
taken over: protection by provenance
operator-created top-level sessions never sleep automatically
not taken over: session-level destroy policy; removal of
population auto_down / auto_destroy (separate decisions)
Alternatives considered, not chosen
separate activity event or session column
a second durable answer overlapping the status log
headless-only idle confirmation
would exclude interactive runtimes that already write ""
population eviction predicate for resume
the waking inbound is newer than "", so every wake resumes
